policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere מְלָשְׁנִי and ketiv מלושני differ only in orthography/vocalization of the same participle 'slanderer' (poel of לשׁן); ASV 'Whoso privily slandereth' renders that sense and carries no italic supply or textual note on the word, so the English permits both readings and the qere base fallback carries the projection.
